evidence: app/src/app/app.routes.ts:48 — abilities route is one deletable entry, page components are one-file dirs
app/src/server/loaders.ts:455 — but each page also has a switch case plus a loader fn (loadAbility at :438) to delete
app/src/app/shared/models.ts:100 — and a VM interface (AbilityVM) that must be removed separately
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.html:72 — plus the inbound links in the Pokémon page template
removability.rationale: Removing a feature means five scattered but mechanical edits (route, page dir, loader+switch, VM, inbound links); nothing is entangled, but the feature isn't self-contained in one directory either.

evidence: app/src/app/shared/pokemon-card.ts:37 — sprite URL derived in one computed; every list (home, move, ability, type, team) feeds ids into this component
app/src/server/loaders.ts:99 — toCards normalizes species-vs-pokémon refs, alternate forms and dex order once, shared by move/ability/type lists
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/move-table.ts:85 — sorting and aria-sort logic lives entirely in the table component
changeability.rationale: The sprite-class bug has exactly one fix site that covers every list, and cross-page logic is normalized server-side; docked one point because the card-grid markup itself is triplicated, so presentational changes land in three templates.

evidence: app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:23 — PAGE_DATA_LOADER injection token cleanly separates browser fetch from server build
app/src/app/app.config.server.ts:12 — server overrides the loader in one config; components never know SSR from client
app/src/app/app.routes.ts:11 — resolver indirection means page components take only a vm input (e.g. app/src/app/pages/type/type-page.ts:14)
app/src/app/app.routes.ts:16-19 — team query-string building duplicated with app/src/app/pages/team/team-page.ts:73
app/src/app/page-title-strategy.ts:17 — title strategy reads the implicit 'vm' route-data contract and VM title field
coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with clear seams: dumb components, VMs over the wire, explicit server/client split. The stringly-typed page-data path contract between routes and the loader switch, plus a duplicated query builder, are the tangles.

evidence: app/src/app/shared/card-list.ts:8 — CardList can't take types or extra per-item content, so it isn't used by home or team
app/src/app/pages/home/home.html:36 — home re-copies the ul.card-grid/li/PokemonCard markup to show type badges
app/src/app/pages/team/team-page.ts:25 — team copies it a third time for remove buttons
app/src/app/shared/pokemon-card.ts:22 — PokemonCard itself stretches well (optional types, hidden, priority inputs)
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/move-table.ts:52 — MoveTable handles the level-up variation via computed columns, no flags
app/src/server/loaders.ts:443 — loadPageData switch is a regular, additive seam: an Items section copies the Moves pattern without touching existing cases
abstraction_design.rationale: The data layer and shared components are built around real variation and extend cleanly, but CardList doesn't stretch to the two lists that need extras, so its markup is copy-pasted three times — exactly where the 'add sorting everywhere' scenario hurts.

findings.issue: The card-grid markup (count line + ul.card-grid + li + app-pokemon-card) is duplicated in three places: card-list.ts:11, home.html:36, team-page.ts:25, because CardList supports neither type badges nor per-item extras like a remove button.
findings.suggestion: Give CardList a types input and an ng-content slot for per-item extras (or a `app-pokemon-card` projection point) so home and team reuse it; any card-grid change then lands once.

findings.issue: Page-data paths ('/pokemon/<name>?game=…') are stringly typed in route resolvers and re-parsed by a switch in app/src/server/loaders.ts:443; a typo compiles and silently renders Not found at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Centralize path builders (next to loadPageData or in page-data.ts) so each page's path is constructed and consumed in one typed place.

findings.issue: Team query-string building (names → '?names=…&names=…') is duplicated in the teamData resolver and again in team-page.ts:73's load().
findings.suggestion: Export one buildTeamPath(names) helper and use it in both places.

findings.issue: The default API base 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated here and in app/src/server/api-client.ts:13; changing the default means editing two files in sync.
findings.suggestion: Define the default once (e.g. export from a small constants module) and import it in both.

findings.issue: Caching rules are spread across three independent caches: server API cache (TTL_MS/MAX_ENTRIES), the client page-data cache (CLIENT_TTL_MS in page-data.ts:16), and the /_data Cache-Control header in server.ts:34.
findings.suggestion: Group the TTL/cache knobs in one documented place or at least cross-reference them; they're legitimately separate layers but should be discoverable together.

findings.issue: The title strategy implicitly couples to the 'vm' route-data key and the VM's title field; a page that resolves under a different key or names the field differently gets the wrong title with no compiler error.
findings.suggestion: Type the route-data contract (e.g. a RoutePageData interface) or derive the heading from a title field on a shared VM base type.

summary: A well-layered app with an exemplary server/client seam: dumb components consume compact VMs, all data logic is normalized server-side in one loaders file, and single-sourced components (PokemonCard, MoveTable, toCards) mean most fixes land in one place. The main editability cost is that CardList doesn't stretch, so card-grid markup exists in three copies, and the stringly-typed page-data path contract between routes and the loader switch is the weakest seam. Extending with new sections (Items) is cheap and follows a regular pattern.
